messages:
sam: Heads-up - customer (EU fintech) reporting a sudden spike in latency and intermittent 401s for API calls since ~08:10 UTC. They say traffic is landing in us-west despite being in the EU. Trace: trace_id=8a3f-xx. Any quick checks?

marta: Can you paste one request id + upstream IP? Also which hostname they hit (api.redwood.ai or regional)? :eyes:

sam: They use api.redwood.ai (no region prefix). Example: request_id=8a3f-2, upstream ip=34.120.45.12, x-region: us-west1, sample curl:

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Request-ID: 8a3f-2"
<snip>
> Connected to api.redwood.ai (34.120.45.12) port 443
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< x-region: us-west1
```

They see 401s and higher latency (~800ms p95 vs normal 120ms). Billing alert: egress looks higher (cross-region).

alex: Quick DNS check from a public resolver (me):

```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
34.120.45.12
34.120.45.13
```

But from an EU resolver I queried (1.1.1.1) it returned the same us-west IPs. TTL from our anycast layer is 300s.

ingrid: This smells like resolver cache affinity at ISP or intermediate caching layer returning stale mapping for some clients. Could also be stale GeoIP DB on the edge that assigned that IP to us-west when it should be EU. @dns-bot any recent GeoIP pushes?

dns-bot: Automated notice: GeoIP city-to-region mapping update deployed 2h ago to edge LB nodes. Propagation completions: 78%. Some legacy POPs still reporting pre-update DB.

marta: If some POPs are still on old mapping, client's resolver could have cached the corresponding anycast answer and keep routing to the wrong POP until TTL expires or client flushes. Do we have ISP/resolver IP from the customer?

sam: Customer provided resolver ip 92.40.12.77 (ISP in DE). They ran `dig +short api.redwood.ai @92.40.12.77` and got the us-west IPs. They also ran `curl --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:34.120.45.12 ...` to force EU and that fixed latency/401s for them.

alex: Repro steps for infra: run a probe from that resolver ASN or spin a VM in eu-west1 and query the ISP resolver to see TTL. Also check our edge logs for incoming source IP and x-region mismatch.

ingrid: Actionable short-term workaround: ask customer to use eu.api.redwood.ai or add the region header to pin requests. Long-term: we need to mitigate resolver affinity by ensuring updated IP sets are announced consistently and reduce TTL on anycast answers during rollouts.

support-bot: Note: Created support ticket #SUP-3284, flagged for credits review and assigned to eng-infra.

oncall_jordan: Eng-infra: can you confirm if the recent GeoIP update caused a split-brain mapping for some POPs? If yes, rollback or push fix to remaining POPs and communicate to affected customers.

marta: I'm seeing partial rollback logs for one edge POP in eu-central that failed the DB apply. Escalating to ops. In the meantime I've told the customer to switch to eu.api.redwood.ai and we've suggested a DNS cache flush on their side. :thumbsup:

sam: Customer confirmed switching to eu.api.redwood.ai removed 401s and latency back to normal. They've requested a credit for the extra egress.

ingrid: Follow-ups: (1) ops to finish GeoIP DB push and validate all POPs (2) eng-infra to add monitoring alert for region mismatch ratio >1% (3) support to process credit for SUP-3284.

alex: For postmortem, collect: dig outputs from affected resolvers, edge apply logs, BGP/announcements at time window, and any TTL values seen.

oncall_jordan: I'll keep incident open until propagation hits 100% and metrics normalized. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: Thanks team — customer happy for now, keeping ticket open for credits and root cause.
